metadata.title: BC atlas — typed origin and change events for Crown corporations and agencies (R02/R06)
metadata.shape: package event_seeds.json shape with atlas: ids, subject_id (local HISTORICAL_BODIES id or null), subject_key (local id or proposed key), evidence.source_url + evidence.locator + evidence.quote instead of package source ids

conventions.date_precision: kept as stated by source; year-only never expanded to January 1
conventions.ranges: end given with range_end_inclusive=true for year/month/day ranges
conventions.assent_vs_in_force: statute assent, in-force and organisational establishment are separate events; 'In force by regulation/proclamation' with unknown date is listed as a gap, not guessed
conventions.reporting_lines: none inferred; related_subjects list only bodies named in the source text

events.title: Workmen's Compensation Act passed (not in force until 1917), per WorkSafeBC

evidence.locator: Our origins > Our history, paragraph beginning "The province's Workmen's Compensation Act"
evidence.quote: The province's Workmen's Compensation Act was passed in 1902, but it did not come into force until 1917 when the Workmen's Compensation Board ... was finally created.

events.interpretation_notes: Retrospective organisational claim; historians distinguish the 1902 employer-liability statute from the 1916 Act that created the Board. Verify against the statute before using as a legal-origin date. Not an establishment date.

events.title: Workmen's Compensation Act (1916) enacted; Board to be a body corporate

evidence.locator: S.B.C. 1916, c. 77, header date (PDF p. 1); Board section (PDF p. 24)
evidence.quote: [31st May, 1916.] ... "Board" shall mean Workmen's Compensation Board ... shall consist of three members to be appointed by the Lieutenant Governor in Council, and shall be a body corporate.
evidence.publisher: BC Laws (King's Printer) historical statute scan

events.interpretation_notes: Date in the chapter header (read from page image). CONFLICT/CLARIFICATION: WorkSafeBC says the Act was "passed in 1902"; s. 75 of this 1916 Act repeals an earlier "Workmen's Compensation Act" (R.S.B.C. 1911, c. 244), so the 1902 date refers to a different, earlier statute. The Board was created by the 1916 Act.

events.title: 1916 Act takes effect generally (except compensation provisions)

evidence.quote: Except as provided in subsection (1), this Act shall take effect on the first day of October, 1916.
evidence.publisher: BC Laws (King's Printer) historical statute scan

events.interpretation_notes: Board provisions could operate from this date (appointments before claims start); first appointment dates not in sources reviewed.

events.title: Compensation provisions take effect; earlier Workmen's Compensation Act and Employers' Liability Act repealed

evidence.quote: The application of this Act as between employers and workmen and as to the payment of compensation in respect of injuries to workmen shall take effect on the first day of January, 1917.
evidence.publisher: BC Laws (King's Printer) historical statute scan

events.interpretation_notes: Consistent with WorkSafeBC 1917-01-01 start.

conflicts.note: Legal vs operational vs retrospective; keep all.

claims: local established 1962-03-31 (unverified; Act in force by proclamation)
WorkSafeBC: Act 'passed in 1902' but not in force until 1917
Statute: Workmen's Compensation Act S.B.C. 1916 c.77 (31 May 1916) created the Board and repealed an earlier Act of the same name (RSBC 1911 c.244)
Government Liquor Amendment Act 1973 replaced the LCB with a general manager (assent 1973-04-18; proclamation unknown)
Liquor Distribution Act 1975 establishes the branch named 'Liquor Distribution Branch' (assent 1975-06-26; proclamation unknown)

conflicts.issue: 1964 is a rename, not a new body; name collision with 2003 B.C. Ferry Authority
claims: S.B.C. 1964 c.57: Toll Highways and Bridges Authority known as British Columbia Ferry Authority from 1964-04-01
Coastal Ferry Act 2003 creates a different 'B.C. Ferry Authority'
assent 1972-03-30 (statute; s.43 of current Act uses 'before March 30, 1972')
Land Commission Amendment Act 1977 assented 1977-09-27 (continues Provincial Land Commission as Provincial Agricultural Land Commission; in-force date unknown)
Act retitled 'Innovation and Science Council Act' 2003-03-12
constituted a corporation effective end of 1995-03-31
current PavCo formed 2008-04-01 by amalgamation (annual reports)
local shows continuous body from 1984 (1984 incorporation not found in official sources reviewed)

gaps: ICBC: proclamation/in-force date of the 1973 Act; Autoplan start day (secondary sources say 1974-03-01, not confirmed in an ICBC/official source); any dated ICBC logo/brand changes; executive appointments.
BCLC: in-force date of Lottery Corporation Act 1985; date of continuation under Gaming Control Act 2002; executive appointments; any dated logo change.
BC Housing: when the operating name 'BC Housing' was adopted; logo history; executive appointments.
BC Transit: proclamation dates of UTA Act 1978 and 1982 amendment; logo history; Metro Transit Operating Company in-force and end dates.
BC Hydro: BC Hydro Act proclamation date; BC Power Commission first appointments; official (non-retiree) source for 1962 logo; later chairs/CEOs.

BC Ferries: official BC Ferries (company) history page not found; exact first-sailing date 1960 only in secondary sources; Ferry Authority 1964–1977 transition proclamation (BC Reg 556/76 cited by law library only); 2003-onward logos.
BC Rail: official history of 1984 BC Rail Ltd reorganisation and 2004 CN transaction not reviewed; actual share-transfer date after 1918 Act.
WorkSafeBC: first Board member appointment dates (1916-1917); 1974 name-change legal instrument and exact day (local uses 1974-07-01, unverified); logo artwork.
Royal BC Museum/BC Archives: statutory instrument for 1908 Provincial Archives; pre-1987 official name; in-force regulation for Museum Act 2003 (org says April 1, 2003).
Knowledge Network: official source for 1981 launch (only non-official sources found); Open Learning Agency 1988 creation; executive appointments.
Destination BC / Tourism BC: executive appointments; logo changes.

Legal Aid BC: proclamation date of LSS Act (local 1979-10-01); Legal Services Commission in-force date (local 1975-08); exact public launch day of the Legal Aid BC brand (planned mid-March 2020, possibly delayed by COVID-19).
CLBC: executive appointment dates.
Columbia Basin Trust: executive appointment dates beyond chair tenure line.

BC Pavilion Corporation / BC Place: 1984 incorporation of original PavCo; BC Place Ltd incorporation date (certificate 207097); BC Place stadium opening (only secondary); 1987 BC Enterprise Corporation link.
ALC: in-force dates of 1977 amendment and 2002 Act; legal status of the Commission under the Land Reserve Commission Act 1999 (2000–2002).
LCB/LDB: 1921 Government Liquor Act assent and LCB establishment day (local 1921-04-13 unverified); proclamation of 1973 amendment and of Liquor Distribution Act 1975.
BCSC: in-force date of Securities Act 1985 (regulation); superintendent-of-brokers predecessor dates.
FICOM: in-force date of Financial Institutions Act 1989.
Innovate BC: corporate-name (not Act-title) change dates in 2003/2004/2006; merger with Advanced Systems Institute (2004) not found in an official source; executives.
SkilledTradesBC: ITAC and ITA in-force dates (both by regulation); ITAC dissolution date.

Logo/identity changes dated by the organisation itself were found only for WorkSafeBC (package seeds), BC Assessment (1996, 2015), BC Hydro (1962, affiliated source), BC Ferries flag (1960–2003 range) and Legal Aid BC (2020).
